# **D3-HOL-02 — Intelligent Meeting and Action Management with Microsoft Teams Copilot**

DAY 3 · MODULE 12 · COLLABORATE WITH COPILOT — TEAMS

**Business scenario:** Enterprise Project Review and Meeting Governance  
**Organization:** Meridian Global Services  
**Participant role:** Project Operations Coordinator  
**Primary tools:** Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Copilot Chat  
**Execution requirement:** Minimum 60 minutes of active participant work

## **1\. Lab mission**

You are coordinating a transformation project at Meridian Global Services.

The project team regularly conducts meetings involving Operations, Customer Experience, IT, Finance, and regional managers. However, important decisions are getting lost, action owners are unclear, and follow-up activities are inconsistent.

The COO has asked you to improve how project meetings are managed.

Your responsibility is to use Copilot to turn meeting discussions into structured business outputs:

* Meeting summaries.  
* Key discussion points.  
* Decisions and unresolved questions.  
* Action items with proposed owners.  
* Risk and dependency registers.  
* Follow-up communications.  
* A consolidated project meeting record.

**The central learning objective:** Move from a meeting conversation to accountable business execution.

This is not just about asking Copilot to summarize a meeting. Participants will learn how to prepare, capture, analyze, validate, and follow up on meeting outcomes.

## **2\. Product access and execution paths**

One important point before we begin: **Copilot Chat, Copilot in Teams meetings, and Teams Intelligent Recap have different capabilities and licensing requirements.**

We will design the lab so that participants can complete the assignment even if they do not have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on.

Core lab — all participants

**Path A: Microsoft Teams \+ Copilot Chat**

* Create and organize a Teams meeting.  
* Prepare and share an agenda.  
* Work with a supplied meeting transcript.  
* Paste the transcript into Copilot Chat.  
* Generate meeting summaries, decisions, action items, and follow-up communications.  
* Share the final outputs in the Teams meeting chat.

This is the reliable training path and does not depend on Teams meeting Copilot.

Optional — when licensed and enabled

**Path B: Copilot directly inside Teams**

* Use Copilot during a live meeting.  
* Ask questions about the meeting discussion.  
* Generate meeting notes and identify tasks.  
* Use the meeting Recap tab to review available insights after the meeting.

Availability depends on the Microsoft 365 Copilot license, meeting settings, and administrator policies.

Microsoft documents that Teams Copilot can summarize discussions, identify speakers and action items, and answer questions about meetings. Access to information after the meeting depends on the meeting configuration and whether transcription is available.

Microsoft Support+1

**Important distinction:** Copilot can be configured to work only during a meeting without creating a transcript, but this does not mean the same meeting insights will automatically remain available after the meeting.

Microsoft Support+1

## **3\. Learning objectives**

By completing this lab, participants should be able to:

1. Schedule and prepare a structured Teams meeting.  
2. Create an effective meeting agenda.  
3. Use Copilot to prepare for a meeting.  
4. Extract key topics and decisions from meeting discussions.  
5. Separate confirmed decisions from proposals and unresolved questions.  
6. Identify action items, proposed owners, and deadlines.  
7. Generate structured meeting minutes.  
8. Prepare follow-up communications.  
9. Organize meeting outputs in the Teams meeting chat.  
10. Validate AI-generated notes before distributing them.

# **4\. Business case — Meridian Global Services**

[Leading UK Microsoft Solutions Partner \- Cisilion](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/3SWuczFRrl0b4mmu5k-JWaWn40ej8CoUQNQZltysq1KeGeNyPf8JWTgSIks2bPSaOBSHbsuIUfbnJ3t_vhm5t3SCXC7S1dW2he3vQcKjAUTFrPfB1xdA14N0YK5g4lE7N0OsYnRrm8cuBlI9nTD2nI5bWZmdOex_upAsNf_VA7I?purpose=inline)  
[cisilion.com](https://www.cisilion.com/microsoft/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Meridian Global Services has started an operational improvement initiative after the latest performance review revealed:

* SLA attainment declined from 85% to 70%.  
* Average resolution time increased from 2.1 to 3.8 days.  
* Month-end backlog increased from 180 to 450 cases.  
* Customer satisfaction declined from 4.2 to 3.4 out of 5\.  
* The South region recorded the lowest June SLA attainment.

The COO has scheduled a project review meeting with the following stakeholders:

| Participant | Role | Responsibility |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Maya Sharma | Chief Operating Officer | Executive sponsor |
| Arjun Mehta | Head of Service Operations | Operational ownership |
| Neha Kapoor | Customer Experience Lead | Customer communication |
| David Thomas | IT Service Manager | Ticketing system and process controls |
| Priya Nair | South Regional Manager | Regional operations |
| Rohan Desai | Finance Business Partner | Financial and resource constraints |

The meeting has one objective:

**Agree on practical actions to improve service performance over the next 30 days without additional headcount or a new enterprise platform.**

Your role is to coordinate the meeting, capture its outcomes, and ensure that agreed actions are followed through.

## **5\. Participant source pack**

The following simulated material is used throughout the lab.

### **Source A — Meeting invitation**

**Meeting:** Meridian Global Services — Operational Improvement Review

**Organizer:** Maya Sharma, Chief Operating Officer

**Required attendees:** Service Operations, Customer Experience, IT, South Regional Manager, Finance.

**Meeting objective:** Review current service performance and agree on operational improvement actions.

**Agenda:**

1. Review the latest operational performance.  
2. Discuss backlog and service-level concerns.  
3. Review customer feedback and communication issues.  
4. Discuss regional operational challenges.  
5. Agree on improvement priorities.  
6. Assign owners and deadlines.  
7. Confirm the next review and reporting requirements.

**Expected outputs:**

* Confirmed decisions.  
* Action register.  
* Open questions.  
* Risks and dependencies.  
* Follow-up communication.

### **Source B — Meeting transcript**

Simulated meeting transcript · Meridian Global Services · Operational Improvement Review

This is the main training artifact. Participants will use it to simulate the work Copilot would perform on a real meeting discussion.

```

MEETING: Meridian Global Services - Operational Improvement Review
CHAIR: Maya Sharma, Chief Operating Officer

MAYA SHARMA (COO):
Thank you, everyone. We are here to agree on how we can improve service performance over the next 30 days. Our latest report shows SLA attainment has dropped from 85 percent in January to 70 percent in June. The backlog has increased from 180 to 450. I want us to focus on practical improvements rather than immediately asking for more resources.

ARJUN MEHTA (SERVICE OPERATIONS):
The operations team has been reviewing the backlog. We are seeing more cases remaining open for longer periods. The Parts category appears to be taking longer than other categories. In the June sample, Parts had an average resolution time of 6.5 days. However, we do not yet have a complete breakdown of delay reasons.

NEHA KAPOOR (CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE):
The feedback we received shows that customers are contacting support repeatedly because they do not receive timely updates. Even when a case is eventually resolved, customers are frustrated by the lack of communication. We should standardize how customers are informed when a case is delayed.

MAYA SHARMA:
Agreed that communication needs attention. What can we introduce without purchasing another platform?

NEHA KAPOOR:
We can define a standard update process using the existing ticketing system. For open cases that are delayed, the customer should receive a status update at least once every two business days. I can prepare the communication template and proposed process.

ARJUN MEHTA:
I can support that. Operations should review overdue cases every morning. We can start with a short daily backlog review. We should identify the oldest cases, the current owner, and what is blocking closure.

PRIYA NAIR (SOUTH REGIONAL MANAGER):
The South region has the lowest June SLA attainment at approximately 64 percent. We need to understand whether this is due to scheduling, parts availability, case complexity, or assignment issues. I can review a sample of the overdue cases and provide findings.

MAYA SHARMA:
That makes sense. Let's not assume the reason before the review is completed. Priya, can you provide the initial case review within three business days?

PRIYA NAIR:
Yes, I can provide the initial review within three business days. I will coordinate with Arjun's team to get the case list.

DAVID THOMAS (IT SERVICE MANAGER):
There may also be an issue with incomplete ticket information. Some tickets do not have consistent fields for assignment, delay reason, or next customer update. I need to check the existing configuration and how teams are using it.

MAYA SHARMA:
David, please review the mandatory fields and current process. We should not introduce a new platform. Can you provide your findings within five business days?

DAVID THOMAS:
Yes. I will review the current configuration and process usage, then share the findings within five business days. Any system changes will be subject to the existing change approval process.

ROHAN DESAI (FINANCE):
From a finance perspective, we have no approval for additional headcount or new technology expenditure in this review period. We should focus on existing tools, process improvements, and better operational visibility.

MAYA SHARMA:
Understood. No new headcount or new platform will be part of this initial 30-day plan. We can revisit resource requirements after we have evidence.

ARJUN MEHTA:
For the daily review, I propose that the Operations team maintain an overdue case register with case ID, age, current owner, reason for delay, and next action. We can use the existing reporting process.

MAYA SHARMA:
Agreed. Arjun will own the daily overdue case review and the register. We should review progress weekly.

NEHA KAPOOR:
For customer updates, I will draft a standard message and proposed communication process. The Operations team will need to ensure the latest case status is available before the message is sent.

MAYA SHARMA:
Agreed. Neha will prepare the draft template within three business days. Operations will validate the case status before any customer update is issued.

PRIYA NAIR:
I will work with Arjun to identify the reasons for delay in the South region. We should also check whether the Parts cases are concentrated in particular locations or suppliers.

ARJUN MEHTA:
I can provide the relevant case records. We do not currently have enough evidence to confirm supplier-related causes.

MAYA SHARMA:
Good. Please keep that as an investigation, not a confirmed conclusion.

DAVID THOMAS:
I also suggest a mandatory next-update field for open cases. It would help teams see when the next customer communication is due. I need to confirm whether the current system supports it without configuration changes.

MAYA SHARMA:
Let's treat that as a proposed improvement. David should confirm feasibility before we approve it.

ROHAN DESAI:
We should also make sure that any proposed changes do not create additional manual reporting work for the teams.

MAYA SHARMA:
Agreed. We will review the workload impact during the first weekly review.

ARJUN MEHTA:
Can we confirm the weekly review? I suggest that we meet every Friday to review backlog, SLA performance, customer updates, and blockers.

MAYA SHARMA:
Agreed. We will hold a weekly review every Friday during the 30-day improvement period. Arjun will coordinate the performance update, and each owner will provide their progress.

NEHA KAPOOR:
I would also like the customer feedback themes included in the weekly update so that we are not measuring operational metrics alone.

MAYA SHARMA:
Agreed. Neha will provide a short customer experience update for each weekly review.

ROHAN DESAI:
Before we close, I want to confirm that no financial benefit has been committed. We need a baseline and actual results before quantifying savings.

MAYA SHARMA:
Correct. We will not claim financial savings or guaranteed performance improvement at this stage. The immediate objective is to improve visibility, ownership, and customer communication, while investigating the operational causes.

MAYA SHARMA (CLOSING):
To summarize, Arjun will lead the daily overdue case review and coordinate the weekly performance update. Neha will prepare the customer communication template within three business days and provide weekly feedback themes. Priya will review South region overdue cases within three business days. David will review ticketing fields and process usage within five business days. We will hold a review every Friday. No new headcount or new platform is approved. Any system changes remain subject to existing approval controls.

END OF MEETING.
```

### **Source D — Meeting governance rules**

**Meridian meeting governance standards**

1. Every action must have a clearly identified owner.  
2. Proposed actions must not be recorded as approved decisions.  
3. Deadlines must match what was agreed during the meeting.  
4. Unresolved questions must remain visible.  
5. Financial benefits must not be claimed without evidence.  
6. Customer updates must be based on verified case information.  
7. System changes must follow existing change approval controls.  
8. Meeting notes must be reviewed before distribution.

**Your task:** Create a structured meeting space before the discussion begins.

**What you are learning:** Teams meeting organization, agenda preparation, participant coordination, and meeting governance.

1. Open [Microsoft Teams](https://teams.microsoft.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com).  
2. Sign in using your work or school account.

9. Save the meeting.

## **Exercise 4 — Extract decisions, action items, and ownership**

**Your task:** Convert the minutes into an action register that can be tracked after the meeting.

**What you are learning:** Action extraction, task ownership, deadlines, accountability, and project tracking.

A meeting summary tells people what happened. An action register tells people what must happen next.

**Action**

Use the transcript and meeting minutes from Exercise 3\.

**Prompt 4 — Create the action register**

```
Act as a Senior Project Coordinator.
Extract all actions and commitments from the Meridian Global Services meeting transcript.
Create a structured action register with these columns:
Action ID.
Action description.
Owner.
Supporting team.
Deadline.
Expected deliverable.
Dependency.
Status.
Evidence required for closure.
Also create a separate list of:
Confirmed decisions.
Proposed actions awaiting approval.
Unresolved questions.
Risks requiring monitoring.
Rules:
Use only commitments explicitly supported by the transcript.
Do not invent action owners.
Do not convert a suggestion into an approved task.
Do not invent calendar dates when only relative deadlines were given.
Mark items without confirmed owners as "Owner to be confirmed."

```

| ----- | ----- | ----- |

| Prepare customer communication template | Neha | 3 business days |

| Review ticketing fields and process usage | David | 5 business days |
| Coordinate weekly performance review | Arjun | Every Friday |

## **Exercise 5 — Identify decisions, disagreements, and unresolved questions**

**Your task:** Identify what the meeting actually resolved and what still needs investigation.

**What you are learning:** Decision intelligence, meeting governance, ambiguity detection, and risk identification.

This is a more advanced use case. Copilot may summarize a discussion correctly but still confuse a proposed idea with a final decision.

**Action**

Use the meeting transcript and action register.

**Prompt 5 — Decision and risk analysis**

```
Act as an independent Project Governance Analyst.
Review the Meridian Global Services meeting transcript.
Create four separate sections:
A. Confirmed decisions
What was explicitly agreed?
Who confirmed it?
What does the decision mean operationally?
B. Proposed actions
Which ideas were suggested but not formally approved?
What validation or approval is still needed?
C. Unresolved questions
What information is still missing?
Who should investigate it?
What evidence would resolve the question?
D. Risks and dependencies
What could prevent the agreed actions from being completed?
What controls or follow-ups are needed?
Pay particular attention to the proposed mandatory next-update field. Do not classify it as an approved system change.
Do not invent additional decisions, approvals, or risks unrelated to the discussion.

```

**Meeting transcript:**

\[Paste Source B\]

Copy prompt  
![][image7]

**Participant activity**

Check whether Copilot has incorrectly promoted any suggestion into an approved decision.

**Expected outcome:** A decision log and unresolved-question register that prevent misunderstandings after the meeting.

## **Exercise 6 — Prepare stakeholder-specific follow-up communications**

**Your task:** Convert the meeting outcomes into clear communications for each stakeholder.

**What you are learning:** Audience-specific communication, follow-up writing, accountability, and professional business messaging.

Different participants need different information. The COO needs the overall outcome. An action owner needs their task and deadline. The wider team needs the shared decisions and next meeting details.

**Action**

Use the action register and decision log.

**Prompt 6 — Generate meeting follow-up communications**

```

Identify the key actions and owners.
Highlight unresolved issues.

Communication 3 — General meeting follow-upPrepare a message for all attendees summarizing the meeting outcomes, the action register, and the next review arrangement.

Use professional business language.
Do not invent approvals.
Do not change deadlines.
```

**Your task:** Make the meeting outputs accessible to the project team.

### **Step 1 — Open the meeting chat**

Post the general follow-up message in the meeting chat.

Do not share unreviewed AI-generated content as an official company decision record.

**Participant activity**

Check that the meeting chat contains:

* Meeting summary.  
* Confirmed decisions.  
* Action register.  
* Unresolved questions.  
* Follow-up communication.

**Expected outcome:** One organized Teams conversation containing the important meeting outputs.

# **7\. Final quality assurance — Validate the meeting record**

**Your task:** Ensure that the AI-generated meeting outputs accurately represent what the participants agreed.

This is where Module 14, Responsible and Effective Use, is also introduced in practice.

A meeting summary can look professional while still creating serious operational problems if it assigns the wrong owner, changes a deadline, or records a proposal as an approved decision.

### **Step 1 — Run an independent review**

Provide the transcript, meeting minutes, decision log, and action register to Copilot Chat.

**Prompt 8 — Audit the meeting outputs**

```
Act as an independent Project Governance Auditor.
Compare the generated meeting minutes, decision log, and action register against the original Meridian Global Services meeting transcript.
Review for:
Incorrect participant attribution.
Missing or incorrectly recorded decisions.
Proposals incorrectly recorded as approved.
Incorrect action owners.
Incorrect deadlines.
Missing dependencies.
Unresolved questions incorrectly presented as resolved.
Unsupported financial or operational claims.
Create an audit table with:
Issue identified.
Affected meeting output.
Evidence from the transcript.
Severity: Critical, Important, or Minor.
Recommended correction.
Do not rewrite the meeting outputs. Identify errors and explain how to correct them.

```

**Original transcript:**

\[Paste Source B\]

**Generated meeting outputs:**

\[Paste your minutes, decision log, and action register\]

Copy prompt

### **Step 2 — Correct the meeting outputs**

Review the audit findings and manually correct the minutes, decision log, and action register.

### **Step 3 — Complete the validation checklist**

**Meeting quality checklist**

0/9  
All meeting participants and roles are correctly identified.  
The executive summary reflects the actual discussion.  
Confirmed decisions are separated from proposals.  
Action owners match the original transcript.  
Deadlines match the original transcript.  
Unresolved questions remain visible.  
No financial savings or guaranteed outcomes have been invented.  
Meeting communications are suitable for their intended audiences.  
The final meeting record has been reviewed before sharing.  
Reset checklist

**Expected outcome:** A validated meeting record that can be shared with the project team.

# **8\. Trainer's validation reference**

Use this section to assess whether participants have interpreted the meeting correctly.

## **A. Confirmed decisions**

| Decision | Confirmation |
| ----- | ----- |
| Daily overdue case review | Approved; Arjun owns it |
| Overdue case register | Approved; Arjun owns it |
| Customer communication template | Neha will prepare it within 3 business days |
| South region overdue case review | Priya will complete initial review within 3 business days |
| Ticketing fields and process review | David will complete findings within 5 business days |
| Weekly performance review | Every Friday during the 30-day period |
| Customer experience update | Neha will provide an update at weekly reviews |
| Additional headcount | Not approved |
| New enterprise platform | Not approved |
| Financial savings claims | No savings commitment made |

## **B. Proposed action, not yet approved**

**Mandatory next-update field in the ticketing system**

David suggested the field. However, he must first confirm whether the existing system supports it and whether a change is needed.

Participants must not record this as an approved system change.

## **C. Important unresolved questions**

* What are the actual reasons for Parts-related delays?  
* Are South region delays related to scheduling, assignment, parts, or case complexity?  
* Are ticket fields consistently populated?  
* Can the current ticketing system support a next-update field without a configuration change?  
* What is the workload impact of daily backlog reviews?

## **D. Expected action register**

| ID | Action | Owner | Deadline |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| A01 | Establish daily overdue review and register | Arjun | Daily |
| A02 | Prepare customer communication template | Neha | 3 business days |
| A03 | Review South region overdue cases | Priya | 3 business days |
| A04 | Review ticketing fields and process usage | David | 5 business days |
| A05 | Coordinate weekly performance review | Arjun | Every Friday |
| A06 | Provide customer experience update | Neha | Every Friday |

The transcript does not establish a specific calendar date for the deadlines. Participants should preserve the relative timeframes.

# **9\. Final participant deliverables**

At the end of the lab, every participant should have produced the following:

**1\. Teams meeting setup**

A scheduled practice meeting with a clear purpose, agenda, and expected outcomes.

**2\. Meeting preparation brief**

Discussion questions, stakeholder priorities, and expected decisions.

**3\. Meeting minutes**

A structured record of participants, topics, decisions, and unresolved questions.

**4\. Action register**

Action IDs, owners, deadlines, deliverables, dependencies, and closure evidence.

**5\. Decision and risk log**

Confirmed decisions, proposed actions, unresolved questions, and risks.

**6\. Follow-up communications**

Executive update, owner-specific messages, and general meeting follow-up.

**7\. Teams meeting chat**

An organized conversation containing the reviewed meeting outputs.

**8\. Quality audit**

Evidence that meeting records and action assignments were checked against the original discussion.

# **10\. Trainer assessment rubric**

| Assessment area | Weight |
| ----- | ----- |
| Meeting setup and agenda | 10 |
| Meeting preparation | 10 |
| Accuracy of meeting minutes | 20 |
| Decision identification | 15 |
| Action extraction and ownership | 20 |
| Follow-up communications | 10 |
| Teams collaboration and sharing | 5 |
| Responsible AI validation | 10 |
| **Total** | **100** |

Suggested assessment:

* **90–100:** Excellent — accurate, structured, and accountable meeting management.  
* **75–89:** Strong — good output with minor gaps.  
* **60–74:** Developing — understands summarization but needs better decision and action validation.  
* **Below 60:** Needs improvement — significant errors in ownership, decisions, or meeting records.
